What color of annunciator signifies a condition that must be dealt with immediately?
What color of annunciator signifies a condition that must be monitored?

water, carbon tetrachloride, carbon dioxide, and dry chemical.

evacuating the indicating element with CO2.

Smoke detectors which use a measurement of light refraction in the air are called
When air samples contain carbon monoxide, the tan-color portable carbon monoxide detectors will turn which color?

choices: Pressure switch and check tee valve.
questions.question: What retains the nitrogen charge and fire-extinguishing agent in a high rate of discharge (HRD) container?
Which fire extinguishing agent is considered to be the least toxic?

The proximity sensor operates on what principle?

Which of the following functions does a skid control system perform?
1. Normal skid control
2. Normal braking.
3. Fail-safe protection.
4. Locked-wheel skid control.
5. Touchdown protection.
6. Takeoff protection.

equalizes the hydraulic pressure in adjacent brakes.

questions.question: In a brake anti-skid system, when an approaching skid is sensed, and electrical signal is sent to the skid control valve which

An anti-skid system consists of basically of three components:
1. Wheel speed sensors
2. Control box
3. Control valves

choices: the landing gear down and lock switch is open.
the landing gear squat switch is open.

questions.question: In flight with the anti-skid armed, current cannot flow to the anti-skid control box because
The _________ provides a mechanical warning to the pilot when a stall condition is imminent.
The reed-type stall warning system installed in some light aircraft is activated by

questions.explanation: An avionics bay contains energized electrical equipment. PPT slide 4: Class C fires are electrical fires involving energized equipment (A = solids, B = flammable liquids, D = burning metals such as magnesium).
questions.question: A class __ extinguisher would typically be installed in an avionics bay.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 12: spot detector thermal switches are heat-sensitive units wired in parallel with each other and in series with the indicator lights, so any one switch closing signals a fire.
questions.question: Spot detectors are a type of ____ _____ that are wired in parallel for redundancy.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 13: the thermocouple responds to the RATE of temperature rise. Voltage is produced only when the hot junction heats faster than the reference junction, so a slow overheat produces no warning.
questions.question: The _______ fire detection system works on a rate of temperature rise, and compares that to a reference temperature.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 9: the Fenwal loop is an Inconel tube packed with thermally sensitive eutectic salt. Heat melts the salt, its resistance drops, and current flows between the nickel center conductor and the tube wall. (A thermistor core is what the Kidde system uses.)
questions.question: As a Fenwal fire loop heats, resistance of the ____ ____ drops, allowing current to flow between the nickel conductor and Inconel wall.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 10: dents or kinks in a continuous-loop element can cause intermittent false alarms, because the element is a slender tube routed around the nacelle.
questions.question: The ____ ____ type of fire detection system can easily be kinked or dented.

questions.explanation: FAA-H-8083-31B p.977: a dual-loop system performs the loop switching and decision making that the crew would otherwise do. That function is called automatic self-interrogation.
questions.question: A dual-loop system may have an automatic ____-____ function that senses and removes a faulty loop from the cockpit indication circuit.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 11: the Lindberg/Systron-Donner element is a helium-filled tube. Heating raises the gas pressure until the alarm switch closes; on further heating the core releases hydrogen to signal an actual fire.
questions.question: The Lindberg pneumatic system incorporates ____ and ____ gases within a stainless steel tube.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 15: the light-refraction detector pairs an LED with a photoelectric cell. Smoke particles refract the LED light onto the cell, which then produces the current that triggers the alarm.
questions.question: In the light refraction type of smoke detector, the _____ ___ detects refracted light from the LED due to smoke particles.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 16: the ionization detector alarms on a reduction in ion density flowing between two electrically charged plates. It runs on 28V DC aircraft power.
questions.question: The _______ type of smoke detector signals an alarm when it senses a change in electrical flow across two plates.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 18: carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the cabin and flight deck, especially on reciprocating-engine aircraft with exhaust shroud or combustion heaters, where exhaust gas can leak into the cabin air.
questions.question: On reciprocating engine aircraft with exhaust shroud heaters, ___ ___ detectors are installed in the cockpit and cabin.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 17 and FAA-H-8083-31B p.980: "Optical sensors, often referred to as flame detectors." The processor recognizes the time signatures of known hydrocarbon flames and ignores sunlight and incandescent light wavelengths.
questions.question: The electronic processor for the ____ ___ is programmed to ignore sunlight and incandescent light wavelengths.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 18: the tan indicator dye on the silica-gel crystals turns gray and then black, and the progression from gray to black is proportional to the CO concentration.
questions.question: Portable carbon monoxide detectors will turn ___ or ___ depending on level of CO concentration.

questions.explanation: False. PPT slide 18: a contaminated carbon monoxide test unit is returned to service by installing a NEW indicating element, not by heating the old one.
questions.question: The indicating element in a CO detector can be restored to service by controlled heating in an oven. True or False?

questions.explanation: PPT slide 20: modern built-in systems are charged with Halon 1301 or 1211. Halon 1301 (bromotrifluoromethane) is the least toxic and the most common; agents such as Halon 1011 (bromochloromethane) are more toxic.
questions.question: Despite its ozone-depleting characteristic, the most common low toxicity extinguishing agent currently used is Halon _____.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 24: high-rate discharge (HRD) bottles are spherical containers charged with a halogenated hydrocarbon agent and pressurized with nitrogen.
questions.question: The ___ ___ ____ spherical bottle are filled with halogenated hydrocarbons and nitrogen.

questions.explanation: FAA-H-8083-31B p.985: the thermal discharge indicator is connected to the container relief fitting and ejects a RED disc when the contents dump overboard because of excessive heat. Yellow means the crew discharged it deliberately; green means the system is ready for use (PPT slide 26).
questions.question: If an extinguisher bottle has overheated, a ___ ___ connected to the relief fitting line will be ruptured or missing.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 25: the squib (also called the cartridge) is an electrically actuated explosive device that breaks the seal on the HRD bottle to release the agent.
questions.question: The explosive device on the fire bottle that releases the extinguishing agent is called the ____ or ___.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 26: an intentional discharge blows out the YELLOW disc on the side of the fuselage, so its absence indicates the crew fired the system. A missing RED disc would instead mean a thermal (overheat) discharge.
questions.question: An intentional discharge of the extinguishing system will be indicated by the absence of what?

questions.explanation: True. PPT slide 24: if the pressure, corrected for ambient temperature, is not between the minimum and maximum limits, the container must be replaced rather than serviced.
questions.question: During an inspection, you notice an APU fire bottle pressure is low. You cannot service it, it must be replaced. True or False?

questions.explanation: False. PPT slide 25: a cartridge removed from a discharge valve must not be used in another discharge valve assembly. The contact point protrudes a different distance on each unit, so a mismatched pair may not make continuity.
questions.question: If multiple discharge valves and squibs are disassembled, mixing and matching is allowed. True or False?

questions.explanation: PPT slides 5-6: the takeoff warning system is armed by a switch on the thrust lever. If the trim, speed brakes, or flaps are not set for takeoff when the thrust lever is advanced, an aural warning sounds.
questions.question: When throttles are advanced during takeoff roll with improper flaps, speed brakes, and stab trim settings, the ___ warning system will activate to alert the aircrew.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 4: the stick shaker uses an imbalanced motor to physically shake the control column and alert an inattentive crew. (The stick pusher instead moves the column forward.)
questions.question: The ____ _____ provides a mechanical back and forth motion warning, alerting the pilot of an imminent stall condition.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 14: a proximity sensor works magnetically with an electromagnet and a ferrous target. When the target comes into range the magnetic field is absorbed and the reference voltage sent to the gear logic unit is reduced.
questions.question: When the target comes within range of the _____ _____, a reduced voltage is detected by the gear logic unit.

questions.explanation: FAA-H-8083-31B p.754: barber pole displays are used when a gear is not up or down and locked, and blinking indicator lights likewise mean gear in transit.
questions.question: During gear retraction or extension, the indicators may blink or may show diagonal lines, commonly known as a ____ ______.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 12: autosyn transmitters and indicators use ELECTROmagnet rotors. Magnesyn systems use permanent magnet rotors instead.
questions.question: In the ______ remote indicating system, an electromagnet is attached to the rotor shaft of the transmitter and indicator.

questions.explanation: FAA-H-8083-31B p.791: each wheel is monitored for a deceleration rate faster than a preset rate. PPT slide 19: the system holds the wheel just below the skid point, which gives the most effective braking.
questions.question: During maximum effective braking on an aircraft, the wheel speed is just below a preset allowable rate of _______.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 11: magnesyn systems use permanent magnet rotors. The transmitter magnet is usually larger than the indicator magnet, but the indicator rotor still adopts the same angle of deflection.
questions.question: In the magnesyn remote indicating system, the rotor uses a ____ ____.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 21: in-flight failures cannot be duplicated at the parking spot, so an anti-skid test set is used to simulate wheel-speed transducer output, deceleration rates, and flight or ground parameters.
questions.question: An anti-skid ____ ___ can simulate transducer outputs, flight/ground parameters, and deceleration rates for system operational checks.

questions.explanation: PPT slides 8-9: in a DC selsyn transmitter a rotatable contact arm feeds voltage through its brushes into a circular resistance winding, which is tapped off in three places about 120 degrees apart.
questions.question: In a ___ ___ transmitter, the resistance winding receives voltage from the contact arm through the brushes.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 18: once the strut extends (weight off wheels) the squat switch - also called the gear safety, ground safety, or WOW switch - tells the anti-skid control box to de-energize the valves, so the anti-skid system is deactivated no matter how the cockpit switch is set.
questions.question: On takeoff, after weight-off-wheels (strut extension), the ___ ___ system is deactivated, regardless of the switch position in the cockpit.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 14: typical GA aircraft and older large transports use cost-effective microswitches to sense gear position. Many modern transports use proximity sensors instead, which removes the wear and corrosion failure points.
questions.question: The conventional means of sensing landing gear position is the low-cost __________.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 4: the stick pusher physically moves the control column forward, pushing the nose down to correct the stall. The stick shaker only vibrates the column as a warning.
questions.question: The ____ _____ drops the aircraft nose to prevent a stall condition.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 3: as the angle of attack nears a stall, low pressure over an opening in the wing leading edge creates a suction that audibly vibrates a reed - the same principle as a woodwind instrument.
questions.question: The ___-___ stall warning device operates on the same principle as a woodwind instrument.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 2: the probe-type sensor feeds dissimilar air pressures against an internal paddle, which repositions a potentiometer. The vane-type instead rotates with the relative wind to reposition the pot directly.
questions.question: The probe-type sensor picks up differing air pressures that act on a paddle, which in turn moves a __________.

questions.explanation: PPT slide 7: the ECAM (electronic centralized aircraft monitor) includes a maintenance panel that lets mechanics test the indicating and warning systems through a built-in test equipment (BITE) function.
questions.question: A maintenance panel is included in the ______ system, and it contains built-in test capability for mechanics to perform electronic checks on aircraft indicating and warning systems.

questions.explanation: MACS supplement slide 2: the cartridge/squib holds an explosive charge and even a small arcing voltage can fire it, so every source of static electricity must be removed - hence grounding wrist straps and natural-fiber clothing rather than synthetics.
questions.question: An important consideration when working with HRD bottle squibs is to eliminate _______ _____ from your person.
source: AMT231 – Assignment – Fire Protection/Pos & Warning – Q1

questions.explanation: True. MACS supplement slide 3: green means a satisfactory or normal condition, for example gear down and locked. At cruise the gear is retracted, so a green gear indication would be wrong.
questions.question: Landing gear indicators should not be illuminated green while the aircraft is at cruise altitude. True or False.
source: AMT231 – Assignment – Fire Protection/Pos & Warning – Q2

questions.explanation: MACS supplement slide 3: white (or any color other than red, yellow, or green) is advisory data that provides operational information, typically text or numbers.
questions.question: White-colored indications present operational information, also known as _______ data.
source: AMT231 – Assignment – Fire Protection/Pos & Warning – Q3

questions.explanation: MACS supplement slides 3-4: red is a WARNING and requires immediate attention or corrective action. Yellow is the CAUTION color, and that is the one meaning a serious condition to be monitored.
questions.question: If the Master Warning light illuminates in flight, there is a discrepancy requiring ______ ______.
source: AMT231 – Assignment – Fire Protection/Pos & Warning – Q4

questions.explanation: False. MACS supplement slide 4: you press the Master light FIRST to acknowledge and extinguish it, then scan the panels to find the lit annunciator. You do not wait until the discrepancy is repaired.
questions.question: The Master Caution switch light should be pressed to extinguish the light only after the discrepancy has been repaired. True or False.
source: AMT231 – Assignment – Fire Protection/Pos & Warning – Q5
